title: Path acceptance condition
statement: A Boolean list $x$ satisfies the acceptance condition if there exist natural numbers $n,s,t$ such that the unary block condition holds with parameters $0,n$, the matrix block condition holds with parameters $n,0$, $s<n$, and the doubled encoding of the binary digits of $s$ begins at index $2n+2+2n^2+2$. Also, $t<n$, the plain encoding of the binary digits of $t$ begins at index $2n+2+2n^2+2+2\ell+2$, where $\ell$ is the number of binary digits of $s$, and there is a walk from $s$ to $t$ of length at most $n$ using the encoded path relation on an $n$-by-$n$ vertex set.
hypotheses_covered: Doubled encoding of Nat.bits(s) begins at the specified index
Plain encoding of Nat.bits(t) begins at the specified index
A walk of length at most n connects s to t using pathEdge(x,n) on n vertices
caveat: The supplied material omits the definitions of the doubled and plain encodings and of the walk predicate, so their exact meanings and the precise walk bound cannot be fully rendered.
